summary: npm package ships obfuscated browser-side account-takeover exploit targeting a specific WordPress site
details: The package's main entry i.js (and its readable sibling original.js) is a browser-context exploit that activates only when window.location.href contains 'noviembrenacional.com'. When loaded in that context it base64-encodes document.outerHTML and POSTs it to a canarytokens.com URL, then uses the current logged-in session (fetch credentials:'include') to either delete other users' accounts via /members/<user>/settings/delete-account/ or, for the target user 'noviembrenacional', change the account email to nyxalor_25@proton.me and take over the account via /my-account/editar-cuenta/. i.js is an obfuscated variant of original.js using \uXXXX unicode escapes for every string, reversed-string tricks (e.g. 'moc.lanoicanerbmeivon' reversed to 'noviembrenacional.com'), and dummy XOR arithmetic to hide the payload from casual inspection while retaining full exploit functionality.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
